title: Parading in Baton Rouge, quitting, and working with Tody Harris
summary: Joe never longed to return home except to parade before the kids; he quit the circus in Baton Rouge and played with Tody Harris.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: It's funny. You seem to have pursued this career different from most of the New Orleans-Baton Rouge, whatever-those-towns-were musicians... You were involved in the medicine shows and the circus and all. Did you ever yearn to go back to New Orleans or Baton Rouge? Or you didn't care?
But you did go back to Baton Rouge on the circus...
The only way I wanted to go back to Baton Rouge was to show the kids. Because when I was a kid... This sounds really corny. I used to tell those kids...
When you got back to New Orleans, you went back to New Orleans with the circus, then.
The circus played New Orleans, and my sister lived there and seen them. And when I went to Baton Rouge and finished parading Baton Rouge, I quit -- and stayed in Baton Rouge.
How long did you stay there for?
I stayed around Baton Rouge and went to work with Tody(?) Harris.
That was one of the Baton Rouge bands.
Yeah, that band in Baton Rouge. I might have worked a couple of times with Toots; I don't know. Buddy Petit still was around Baton Rouge, and so was Guy Kelly.
They never did much leave there, then.
They went to New Orleans, went to...
The funny thing about New Orleans musicians, none of them really wanted to leave. If it wasn't for the Storyville closing, none of those guys probably never would have left New Orleans.
